minutes.headline: Committee approved a one-year FY23 salary grid and a new civilian traffic position, and set monthly meetings.
minutes.summary: The Personnel Committee approved a new civilian traffic member job in the Salary Administration Plan with pay set by the police contract, and a Parks board clerk starting grade and step. It debated two versions of a salary grid addressing minimum wage and voted to adopt the cheaper version for FY23 only. It scheduled a March 28 final vote on the SAP text and agreed to meet the first Monday of each month.

what_happened.line: The Personnel Committee voted to adopt a one-year FY23 salary grid only, the second and cheaper of two versions, with roll call all aye as heard.
The committee deferred the FY24-25 grid and grade consolidation to a salary survey to be done this year.
A new civilian traffic member job was placed in the Salary Administration Plan with an asterisk, pay following the police contract detail rate.
The committee voted to hire the Parks Commission board secretary at a set grade and step.
Members were told to send Salary Administration Plan text comments to HR by Wednesday, with a final vote on the text set for March 28; monthly meetings begin May 2.

why_it_matters: The FY23 grid sets the pay scale behind town wage lines, and the second version was chosen partly because it costs less, so it shapes the personnel costs in next year's town budget.
Only FY23 is covered, so pay for later years waits on a salary survey and a later vote, and the Salary Administration Plan text itself still needs a final vote.
watch_next: Final committee vote on the Salary Administration Plan bylaw text, set for Monday, March 28 at five.
Results of the salary survey, which would inform the FY24-25 grid and any grade consolidation.

The one substantive difference is the Parks board clerk's starting step: ours says Grade 6 Step 6 and the official minutes say Step 2. The roles given for Nancy also differ, and the official minutes omit the monthly meeting schedule and the budget dollar figures.
